claims.text: Mechanical-property variation among single-phase FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived alloys is primarily controlled by lattice distortion and local chemical fluctuations rather than constituent count.
The equiatomic quinary alloy and its quaternary and ternary subsets can all be produced as single-phase FCC materials by identical thermomechanical treatments.
Changing from quinary to selected quaternary and ternary compositions can systematically increase or decrease atomic-size mismatch.
Changing atomic-size mismatch changes the degree of lattice distortion.
The proposed composition changes can vary lattice distortion while retaining a single-phase FCC structure.
Mechanical tests will be performed from room temperature to approximately 500°C under controlled strain rates and uniform processing histories.
Lattice distortion and local chemical inhomogeneity modify dislocation-core structures.
Lattice distortion and local chemical inhomogeneity can promote wavy dislocation lines.
Modified dislocation-core configurations affect the mobility of the primary dislocation type.
Greater lattice distortion makes certain dislocations less mobile.
Reduced dislocation mobility increases yield strength.
Excessive lattice distortion reduces ductility by impeding the dislocation motion required for plastic deformation.
Relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline, alloys with greater lattice distortion will have higher yield strength.
Relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline, alloys with greater lattice distortion will have lower ductility.
Alloys with less lattice distortion will have lower strength.
Alloys with less lattice distortion may not exhibit significant gains in ductility.
Mechanical performance has a nonlinear relationship with constituent count.
The proposed mechanism is limited to similarly processed, single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys.
Multiphase or BCC alloys may be governed by mechanisms other than the proposed FCC lattice-distortion mechanism.
Stacking-fault energy and secondary-phase formation may also affect the relationship between lattice distortion, dislocation mobility, and mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The material-initial-state field describes the quinary alloy and its quaternary and ternary subsets as all yielding single-phase FCC structures, whereas the query states that only nine of the 16 candidate alloys are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
